author: Epiphanius of Salamis
addressee: the presbyters and deacons of Syedra in Pamphylia
occasion: Epiphanius writes in response to a request from the clergy of Syedra for a statement of the faith. The source text does not specify the content of their request beyond seeking truth; the emphasis on Trinity and Holy Spirit is Epiphanius's own development in his response.
argument: Epiphanius opens by praising his addressees for seeking the Holy Spirit through their request, seeing it as a sign of God's grace. He states that those who speak in harmony with Peter's confession will be blessed by the Lord, as Peter himself was blessed when he heard 'Blessed are you'. He argues that knowledge of the only true God leads to unity with God and away from polytheism, which scatters human thoughts toward 'such fornication'—for Scripture says, 'the invention of idols is the first fornication'. He insists that Jesus Christ, whom the Father sent, is himself true God, as John says of the Only-Begotten. The section concludes by affirming that the Father is the one true God, because the Only-Begotten is 'only from only' and the Holy Spirit is 'only'—the grammar emphasizes the uniqueness of each person in the Trinity rather than procession 'from' the Father alone.

outline.move: Epiphanius praises the addressees' request, blesses their confession of Christ as Peter was blessed, and argues that the one true God is a Trinity in unity: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.

scripture: Epiphanius quotes the Gospel of John and alludes to Matthew's account of Peter's confession. He uses Septuagint-style language and refers to Scripture generally as 'the Scripture'. Modern citations should use standard English Bible book names and chapter/verse numbering.
uncertain: The exact date of composition is not stated in the text; 374 is the commonly accepted date based on external evidence.
The addressee is not named in this section; the identification of the clergy of Syedra comes from the wider tradition of the work.

_unresolved_facts.claim: The source text does not specify the content of their request beyond seeking truth
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Οὐκ ἀθέους γὰρ ὑμῶν καὶ τῶν καθ᾽ ὑμᾶς αἰτήσεις τὰς διὰ τῶν γραμμάτων ἡγησάμην, ποθεινότατοι, ἀλλὰ τὴν κίνησιν ἐδοκίμασα ἐκ τῆς τοῦ Θεοῦ χάριτος ἐν ὑμῖν ὑπάρξασαν
_unresolved_facts.fix: The source specifies their request was made 'διὰ τῶν γραμμάτων' (through letters) and that Epiphanius judged it not godless but a 'κίνησιν' (impulse/movement) from God's grace; the content is implied to be a request for doctrinal guidance, not merely 'seeking truth' in a vague sense.

_unresolved_facts.claim: the Holy Spirit through their request
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ὃς εὐδόκησε τῇ ὑπερβολῇ τῆς αὐτοῦ ἀγαθότητος ἐν ἅπασι δοῦναι τὸ ἅγιον αὐτοῦ Πνεῦμα τοῖς αὐτὸν ἐν ἀληθείᾳ ζητοῦσιν
_unresolved_facts.fix: Epiphanius praises God's economy in giving the Holy Spirit to those who seek Him in truth; he does not say they sought the Holy Spirit 'through their request' but that God gives the Spirit to those who seek Him in truth, and he sees their letter as evidence of such seeking.

_unresolved_facts.claim: 'such fornication'—for Scripture says, 'the invention of idols is the first fornication'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ἵνα μὴ πολυθεΐα ἐν ἡμῖν ἔτι ᾖ, καὶ ἐπὶ πορνείαν τοιαύτην ἐπισκορπίζηται τὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων νοήματα, ἀλλ᾽ ἐπὶ ἑνότητα τοῦ μόνου ἀληθινοῦ Θεοῦ· Πρώτη γὰρ πορνεία, ἐπίνοια εἰδώλων, φησὶν ἡ Γραφή
_unresolved_facts.fix: The 'such fornication' refers back to polytheism (πολυθεΐα), not forward to idol-invention as a separate category; the structure is: polytheism scatters thoughts toward 'such fornication'—for Scripture says 'the invention of idols is the first fornication.' The 'such' (τοιαύτην) refers to polytheism itself as fornication, with the Scriptural citation providing the grounding.

_unresolved_facts.claim: the grammar emphasizes the uniqueness of each person in the Trinity rather than procession 'from' the Father alone
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ἀλλὰ μόνος ἀληθινὸς Θεός, ἐπειδὴ μόνος ἐκ μόνου ὁ Μονογενής, καὶ μόνον τὸ ἅγιον Πνεῦμα
_unresolved_facts.fix: The grammar emphasizes the Son's unique generation 'ἐκ μόνου' (from the only/alone [Father]), not merely 'uniqueness' in a general sense; the 'μόνον' with the Holy Spirit is grammatically incomplete but parallels the Son's 'from only,' suggesting a shared pattern of divine origin, not just uniqueness of each person.

_unresolved_facts.claim: quoted directly with the words 'Blessed are you, Simon bar Jonah'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Μακάριος εἶ σὺ, Σίμων βὰρ Ἰωνᾶ, τουτέστιν, υἱὲ Ἰωνᾶ
_unresolved_facts.fix: The words are narrated/paraphrased by Epiphanius as what Peter heard, not presented as a direct quotation formula from Jesus; Epiphanius says Peter 'will be blessed' (μακαρισθήσονται) as 'that holy one was blessed hearing' (ὁ ἅγιος ἐκεῖνος ἐμακαρίσθη ἀκούων), with the content introduced by καθὼς, not a direct quote marker.

_unresolved_facts.claim: quoted with slight adaptation from the Gospel of John (John 17:3 with modification: 'ἐν ἑαυτοῖς' instead of 'αἰώνιον', and 'ἀπέστειλεν' instead of 'ἀπέστειλας')
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ἵνα ἔχωσι τὴν ζωὴν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς, τὸ γινώσκειν τὸν μόνον ἀληθινὸν Θεὸν, καὶ ὃν ἀπέστειλεν Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν
_unresolved_facts.fix: The quotation uses 'ἀπέστειλεν' (3rd person) not 'ἀπέστειλας' (2nd person), but more significantly the brief misses that 'ἐν ἑαυτοῖς' replaces 'αἰώνιον' (eternal), and the whole is introduced as Jesus's own words to his disciples ('ἣν ἔδωκεν ὁ μονογενὴς Υἱὸς τοῖς ἑαυτοῦ μαθηταῖς λέγων'), making this a quotation of Jesus, not a direct quotation of John 17:3 with Jesus as speaker in the Gospel context.

_unresolved_facts.claim: introduced with 'as John says about him'
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: ὡς λέγει περὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ Ἰωάννης· Ὁ Μονογενὴς, ὁ ὢν εἰς τὸν κόλπον τοῦ Πατρὸς, αὐτὸς ἐξηγήσατο
_unresolved_facts.fix: The introduction is 'ὡς λέγει περὶ αὐτοῦ ὁ Ἰωάννης' ('as John says about him'), but the content quoted is John 1:18, not a statement that 'Jesus is the Only-Begotten who is in the bosom of the Father' as a description; the brief's 'as John says about him' is close but the rendering should note the exact formula 'ὡς λέγει' not 'as John says about him' as a full quotation formula.

_unresolved_facts.claim: The apostle Peter, whose confession of Jesus as the Christ is cited as the model of blessed faith
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: σύμφωνα λέγειν τῷ μακαριωτάτῳ Πέτρῳ, ὅτι Σὺ εἶ ὁ Χριστὸς ὁ Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ τοῦ ζῶντος, σαφῶς ὑπ᾽ αὐτοῦ τοῦ Κυρίου μακαρισθήσονται
_unresolved_facts.fix: Peter is cited as one who spoke 'in harmony' (σύμφωνα) with the addressees' own confession; the addressees are the ones who will be blessed for speaking in agreement with Peter's words, not Peter being cited as a model for them to imitate. The direction is: the addressees speak in harmony with Peter → they will be blessed as Peter was.
